_comment: MASTER SCHEDULE - single source of truth for PHYS 230/235, Fall 2026.
Times are course-local wall clock (America/Indiana/Indianapolis). Never epochs.
"opens" is the Restrict-access date, which is how this course gates activities;
the quiz-level open date is deliberately left unset throughout.
track: both | calc | alg. Derived from the Moodle group restriction where one exists.
Consumed by: the master-schedule viewer, the course-map generator, and the
pre-class audit. Seeded 2026-09-21 from course-map-fall-26.html + a live Moodle pull.

textbook.current: Knight — all "reading" fields on days are Knight sections
textbook.nextYear: OpenStax, NOT Knight. Every reading needs remapping when this schedule is rebuilt. data/topics.json already carries an OpenStax mapping per topic in sim_readings (University Physics + College Physics), which is the head start for that remap.

sim.name: Oscillation Explorer
sim.note: Sliders for amplitude, period and phase with a live phasor → sine link.

plan.lec: Define amplitude, period, angular frequency ω and phase from x(t)=A cos(ωt+φ).
plan.exp: SHM explorer — drag A, T, φ and watch the curve and a rotating phasor.
plan.prac: Read x(t) graphs and extract all four parameters.

due.label: KO 0
due.note: first-day kickoff; the course map numbering skips day one

sim.name: Energy in SHM — Mass on a Spring
sim.note: Animated mass on a spring with live KE/PE energy bars.

plan.lec: Energy interchange KE↔PE; restoring force F=−kx and a=−ω²x.
plan.exp: Energy-bar sim: watch KE/PE trade as the mass oscillates.
plan.prac: Spring–mass numericals; find ω from k and m.

sim.name: Simple Pendulum
sim.note: Adjustable length / gravity; period read-out and angle trace.

plan.lec: Why a hanging spring is still SHM about a shifted equilibrium; small-angle pendulum.
plan.exp: Pendulum sim — vary length and g, measure the period.
plan.prac: Predict periods; test the small-angle limit.

sim.name: Wave Explorer
sim.note: Equation-driven traveling & standing waves.

plan.lec: y(x,t)=A sin(kx−ωt); v=fλ; superposition → standing waves & nodes.
plan.exp: Wave explorer — build a wave from its equation, then add two for a standing wave.
plan.prac: Graph ↔ equation drills (use the wave quiz).

sim.name: Standing Waves — Strings & Pipes
sim.note: Standing waves on a string or in a pipe — set the ends, step the harmonics.

plan.lec: Wave speed v=√(T/μ); harmonic series on a fixed string.
plan.exp: Standing Waves sim — string and pipe modes, hear/see overtones.

sim.name: Two-Source Interference
sim.note: Draggable sources with a live interference field — reused for diffraction in the optics unit.

plan.lec: Path difference, constructive vs destructive, beats.
plan.exp: Two-source interference sim — drag sources, watch the pattern (you asked for this).

sim.name: E-Fields in Conductors & Insulators
sim.note: Put charge on a conductor or an insulator and see where the field and the excess charge end up.

plan.lec: Charge models, charging by friction/contact/induction, polarization.
plan.exp: Electroscope / charged-rod sim — predict then test.

sim.name: Electrostatic Force Explorer
sim.note: Drag + / − charges and watch field vectors and potential update live. The workhorse sim for electrostatics.

plan.lec: Coulomb’s law; the field idea E=F/q; field of a point charge.
plan.exp: Point-charge field explorer — drop charges, see the vector field.

sim.name: Electric Field Explorer
sim.note: Drop point charges, put a field point anywhere, and add each charge’s E vector to get the total.

plan.lec: Vector superposition of fields; the leap to continuous distributions.
plan.exp: Electric Field Explorer — predict the resultant E by adding each charge’s vector.
plan.prac: Set up and evaluate the field of a line or ring of charge, using symmetry to simplify.

sim.name: Building a Distribution from Point Charges
sim.note: Line / ring / disk with adjustable size and a measurable field point.

plan.lec: Line / ring / disk fields and their far-field limits.
plan.exp: Distribution-field sim — vary size, watch the field approach a point charge.

days.calc: On-axis field of a ring and a disk by integration, then the far-field (point-charge) and infinite-sheet limits.
days.alg: Use the ring / disk / sheet field results as given; decide which limit applies and compare magnitudes.

video.note: Khan Electric flux + Gauss law, or record

sim.name: Gauss’s Law — Flux Through a Closed Surface
sim.note: Adjustable Gaussian surface around charges with live flux read-out.

plan.lec: Dipole moment and torque τ=p×E; flux concept; Φ=q_enc/ε₀; symmetry as the key to using it.
plan.exp: Gauss-flux sim — draw a surface around charges and count flux.

days.calc: Evaluate ∮E·dA for sphere, line and plane symmetries.
days.alg: Use the three symmetry results; reason about enclosed charge and flux.

sim.name: Gauss’s Law — Flux Through a Closed Surface
sim.note: Shape library: sphere, cylinder, pillbox.

plan.lec: Spheres, lines and planes/sheets via symmetry; conductors in equilibrium.
plan.exp: Flux sim with different symmetric shapes.

days.calc: Apply Gauss’s law to a charged sphere, an infinite line and an infinite slab; handle a conductor with an internal cavity.
days.alg: Use the sphere / line / plane field results; reason about where charge sits on a conductor and the field just outside.

plan.lec: Work to assemble charges; U=kq₁q₂/r; energy conservation.
plan.exp: PE-vs-separation sim; release a charge and watch energy convert.

days.calc: Same lesson for both sections; the Calc set is Online HW 8.
days.alg: Same lesson for both sections; Algebra does Written HW 3C instead of the online set.

sim.name: Equipotential Explorer
sim.note: Field explorer in potential mode: equipotential contours ⊥ to field lines.

plan.lec: V=U/q; potential of a point charge; equipotentials; relate E=−dV/dx.
plan.exp: Equipotential + field-line sim — V map, ⊥ field lines, read the gradient.
plan.prac: Add potentials (scalars!) from several charges; go V↔E.

plan.lec: No new content.
plan.exp: Open problem stations; slack to absorb any electrostatics overrun before the test.
plan.prac: Whiteboard the hardest problems from the unit.

sim.name: Circuit builder
sim.note: Drag batteries, resistors and wires; live current/voltage meters. Reused across circuits.

plan.lec: I=ΔV/R; junction and loop rules as charge/energy conservation.
plan.exp: Circuit builder — wire a two-loop circuit and probe it.
plan.prac: Solve a 2-loop network for all currents.

sim.name: Circuit builder
sim.note: Series/parallel reduction focus.

plan.lec: Equivalent-resistance reasoning; voltage/current dividers.
plan.exp: Circuit builder — reconfigure and predict before measuring.
plan.prac: Reduce ladder networks to one resistor.

sim.name: Circuit builder
sim.note: Internal resistance and meters.

plan.lec: Real batteries (internal resistance); ammeter vs voltmeter placement.
plan.exp: Circuit builder with meters — measure correctly vs incorrectly.

sim.name: RC charging sim
sim.note: Capacitor charge/voltage vs time with adjustable R, C and a τ marker.

plan.lec: Charging / discharging; time constant τ=RC; exponential behavior.
plan.exp: RC sim — watch the exponential and mark one time constant.

plan.lec: No new content.
plan.exp: Open problem stations; slack before the circuits test.

sim.name: Magnetic field of currents
sim.note: B field around wires/loops; superpose multiple currents.

plan.lec: B direction by right-hand rule; the Biot–Savart idea.
plan.exp: Field-of-a-wire sim — see B circle the current.

days.calc: Derive B from a current element; integrate for a wire and a loop.
days.alg: Apply B=μ₀I/2πr and the loop-center result; reason from field patterns.

days.topic: B from a line + a loop

sim.name: Magnetic field of currents
sim.note: Two-wire superposition mode.

plan.lec: B=μ₀I/2πr; field at the center of a loop; superposition of wires.
plan.exp: Superpose two wire fields; find the null point.

sim.name: Ampère loop sim
sim.note: Pick an Amperian loop around currents; live circulation read-out.

plan.lec: Circulation; ∮B·dl=μ₀I_enc; Amperian loops. (Pairs with Biot–Savart as the two ways to find B.)
plan.exp: Ampère-loop sim — choose a loop, count enclosed current.

days.calc: Apply ∮B·dl for a wire and a solenoid; justify loop choice.
days.alg: Use the solenoid (B=μ₀nI) and wire results; enclosed-current counting.

sim.name: Dipole field + torque
sim.note: Electric vs magnetic dipole patterns, plus rotate-in-field torque & energy.

plan.lec: Dipole moment; the p↔μ analogy; torque τ=p×E and τ=μ×B; energy U=−μ·B.
plan.exp: Dipole sim — compare E/B dipole fields, then rotate one in a field for torque.
plan.prac: Dipole field + torque/energy problems. (Merged from the old two dipole days.)

sim.name: Lorentz-force particle
sim.note: Charge moving in adjustable E and B; traces helices/circles.

plan.lec: F=qv×B; circular motion; radius r=mv/qB.
plan.exp: Lorentz-force sim — launch a charge into a field, trace the circle.

sim.name: Current-loop / motor
sim.note: Force and torque on a current-carrying loop in a field.

plan.lec: F=IL×B; torque on a current loop → the motor.
plan.exp: Current-loop sim — see the loop torque and spin a simple motor.

sim.name: Lorentz-force + motor stations
sim.note: Velocity selector, cyclotron radius and a spinning current loop — magnetism applications in one place.

plan.lec: Magnetism put to work: mass spectrometer, velocity selector, cyclotron, the electric motor.
plan.exp: Application stations — Lorentz-force sim (mass spec / cyclotron) and the current-loop motor sim.
plan.prac: Multi-step applied problems; a magnetism capstone.

sim.name: Faraday / induction sim
sim.note: Move a magnet or change a field through a loop; live flux, EMF and induced current.

plan.lec: Magnetic flux; Lenz’s law for current direction.
plan.exp: Move-a-magnet sim — push a magnet through a loop, predict the current.

video.note: Crash Course #29 covers it, or record

sim.name: Faraday / induction sim
sim.note: Graph mode: flux and induced EMF vs time.

plan.lec: EMF=−dΦ/dt; motional EMF.
plan.exp: Induction sim with synchronized flux and EMF graphs.

sim.name: Faraday / induction sim
sim.note: Eddy-current and induced-field variants.

plan.lec: Induced electric fields; eddy currents; real-world applications.
plan.exp: Induction sim variants (eddy-current brake).

sim.name: Ray-optics sim
sim.note: Refraction / TIR at an interface plus a dispersion mode; reused for lenses & mirrors.

plan.lec: n₁ sinθ₁=n₂ sinθ₂; critical angle and TIR; why n varies with λ (prisms, rainbows).
plan.exp: Refraction sim — drag the ray across the critical angle, then send white light through a prism.

sim.name: Lens ray-tracer
sim.note: Converging/diverging lenses with principal rays and image formation.

plan.lec: Thin-lens equation 1/f=1/s+1/s′; converging vs diverging; magnification.
plan.exp: Lens ray-tracer — move the object, watch the image form.

sim.name: Mirror ray-tracer
sim.note: Concave/convex mirrors with principal-ray construction.

plan.lec: Mirror equation; principal rays for concave/convex mirrors.
plan.exp: Mirror ray-tracer — trace images for both mirror types.

video.note: Crash Course #31 Diffraction & Interference, or record

sim.name: Diffraction / slit pattern
sim.note: Single/double slit intensity pattern — extends the interference sim.

plan.lec: Double-slit interference; single-slit diffraction; the role of λ.
plan.exp: Diffraction sim — vary slit spacing and wavelength, read the pattern.

sim.name: Diffraction / slit pattern
sim.note: Grating mode: many-slit interference.

plan.lec: Gratings (many slits) sharpen the maxima; resolving power.
plan.exp: Grating sim — add slits, watch maxima sharpen.

video.note: Crash Course #32 Light as a Wave, or record

sim.name: Polarization (Malus) sim
sim.note: Stacked rotatable polarizers with live transmitted intensity.

plan.lec: EM wave structure & the wave equation; Malus’s law for polarizers.
plan.exp: Polarization sim — rotate polarizers, watch intensity follow cos².

days.alg: Connect c=fλ and the EM-wave picture qualitatively; focus on Malus’s law.

plan.lec: No new content (last day of class).
plan.exp: Final review stations across optics + cumulative.
